page: Microsoft Azure E128-64as_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Easv7 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. This virtualized instance, managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, features 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core. It is configured with 1024.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong CPU and memory subsystem performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores rank in the top 10% tier, supported by high-frequency execution and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration. Memory bandwidth is also robust, with cached small-block reads reaching 6708.98 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 203.18 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% tier. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks also rank highly, with Redis handling 96.9 million operations per second.

While the instance delivers top-tier performance for small to medium LLM inference tasks, its execution speed drops to average levels for large 70B models due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware. The lack of local storage requires architectural reliance on external network storage, which may impact latency-sensitive I/O operations. Given its high memory density and strong multi-threaded decompression capabilities, this instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale databases, in-memory caching, data analytics, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
